# Pravdeep Kullar

> Forward Deployed Engineer and full-stack developer based in Ontario, Canada, with over 2 years of hands-on experience in React, Next.js, TypeScript and Node.js, plus Python for ML. Works directly with client teams at Nx Growth Partners to scope AI and software problems into clear milestones and ship them, and was previously a full-stack developer at Mentera, a healthcare AI platform. Holds a graduate certificate in AI with Machine Learning from Humber Polytechnic (2026).

## Experience
- Forward Deployed Engineer, Nx Growth Partners (Feb 2026 to present). Custom software and AI development agency: AI agents, copilots, RAG and knowledge systems, custom web and mobile apps, and integrations into clients' existing stacks.
- Full-Stack Developer, Mentera (Jul 2024 to Dec 2025). Healthcare AI platform for private practices and medspas. Canvas side panel for Tera, the AI chat assistant; config-driven integration drawer covering 35 integrations; Next.js marketing site performance pass.
- Freelance Web Developer, Rosehill Design Build (2026). Next.js marketing site on Vercel; domain and DNS setup; client feedback rounds with the client's COO.
- Web Developer Intern, Rebelsnow (Jan 2024 to Jul 2024). Client e-commerce websites.

## Website services
Freelance website work for small businesses in Ontario, alongside full-time front-end and full-stack roles. The main service is moving businesses off slow, high-maintenance WordPress sites onto fast custom sites built with Next.js and TypeScript and hosted on Vercel. Redesigns for sites that aren't on WordPress are a second offer. Every project starts with a free site review. WordPress migrations and redesigns start at $2,000 CAD, with a fixed quote before work starts and payment split 50% to start and 50% at launch. Custom work past the website, such as a CRM for tracking customers and leads, is also available, quoted separately at a higher price. Most take 2 to 4 weeks from the free review to launch.
- [WordPress migration](https://www.builtbyprav.com/services/wordpress-migration): the main service. Moving off a slow, high-maintenance WordPress site onto a fast custom site built with Next.js and TypeScript on Vercel, with no plugin or security updates, faster load times and fewer things that can break. Every page and form is rebuilt, every old URL that changes gets a permanent (301) redirect, email and DNS settings are checked before the domain switches, and the old hosting stays on for a couple of weeks. Self-editing is an optional paid add-on, quoted separately: the owner gets a login to a simple editing dashboard for text, images and posts, without plugins or layout changes.
- [Website services](https://www.builtbyprav.com/services): overview of the WordPress move and the supporting services, pricing, process and FAQs.
- [Website redesign](https://www.builtbyprav.com/services/website-redesign): for sites that aren't on WordPress. Rebuilding an outdated or slow site around the one thing a visitor came to do: call, book, or ask for a quote, keeping pages that already rank at the same address and redirecting the ones that change.
- [Speed and local SEO](https://www.builtbyprav.com/services/speed-and-seo): measuring Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS) in PageSpeed Insights, fixing what slows a site on phones, then measuring again. Offered as a fixed-price tune-up starting at $750 CAD, and included in every WordPress migration and redesign. Also covers local search basics: the Google Business Profile, a name, area and phone number that match everywhere, and page titles that name the service and the area.
- [Website care](https://www.builtbyprav.com/services/website-care): edits, updates and hosting help after launch, on two month-to-month plans that can be cancelled any time. Basic is $75 CAD a month: software and security updates, backups, uptime monitoring, up to 30 minutes of content edits a month, and a reply within 2 business days. Standard is $150 CAD a month: everything in Basic, plus up to 2 hours of edits a month, a monthly speed check, and a reply within 1 business day.
